learningObjective: Diagnose fairness issues in multi-tenant LLM serving and identify levers that improve fairness without collapsing throughput.
stem: Multi-tenant serving of an LLM shows the following per-user metrics under load. Which mitigations would reduce the unfairness without regressing aggregate throughput below the load's floor. (Choose all that apply.)
profileData:
Two tenants share a serving pool:
  Tenant A (short prompts, ~200 tokens; short outputs, ~50 tokens): TPOT p50 = 55 ms, TTFT p50 = 200 ms
  Tenant B (long prompts, ~4K tokens; long outputs, ~500 tokens): TPOT p50 = 55 ms, TTFT p50 = 4.5 s
  Preemption rate on tenant A: 25%
  Preemption rate on tenant B: 8%
  When tenant B has a burst of arrivals, tenant A's TPOT spikes to 180 ms.
  KV usage: ~90% steady, ~99% during bursts.

options.text: Enable chunked prefill so tenant B's long prefills are broken into chunks that interleave with tenant A's decode iterations; tenant A's TPOT during bursts drops back near the steady-state 55 ms.
Serialize the scheduler to only run one tenant at a time: this eliminates cross-tenant interference and guarantees fair TPOT to whichever tenant is running.
Enforce per-tenant KV budgets or admission quotas so tenant B's bursty long prompts cannot consume more than a bounded fraction of KV, preventing tenant A's preemption rate from spiking.
Add a fairness-aware scheduler (e.g., token-level fair queueing across tenants): prevents one tenant's long-decoding requests from monopolizing decode iterations.

explanation: A is correct: chunked prefill directly solves the burst-driven TPOT spike for tenant A by interleaving decoding with the long prefill of tenant B. C is correct: KV budget quotas cap the contention tenant B can create. D is correct: fairness-aware scheduling addresses long-request domination. B is wrong: serializing tenants collapses aggregate throughput to a single-tenant baseline; the goal is fairness without throughput collapse.
assumptions: Serving stack supports chunked prefill and per-tenant admission control.
Fair-queueing scheduler is available (or can be added).
nonImplications: Does not imply chunked prefill has zero overhead; there is a small per-chunk cost.
Does not imply admission quotas eliminate all bursts; they cap the worst case.

distractorRationales.B: Kills aggregate throughput to gain fairness.
